## Today

**Question:** How did life expectancy change in each continent since 1952?

| Step | What we do |
|------|-----------|
| 1 | Download the Gapminder CSV |
| 2 | Add continent and subregion with `countrycode` |
| 3 | Split, apply, combine |
| 4 | Plot the summary table |

---

# 1. Get the data {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**One CSV from Google Drive**

---

## Download the CSV once

```r
# Run once. It saves a copy of the file in your data folder.
read_csv("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vQMKvrshkL1R55vcnXnXQ14VfJM6HB62bed8U6ukVc-9ncRg79co2GoaS84eb1o4aEg1bqLFiWNJAS3/pub?gid=554197504&single=true&output=csv") |>
  write_csv(here("data", "gapminder.csv"))
```

From now on every chunk reads the file in `data/`. No internet needed.

---

## Look at the table

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  glimpse()
```

---

## Names with capitals are hard to type

```{r}
# clean_names() writes lifeExp as life_exp
here("data", "gapminder.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names() |>
  glimpse()
```

---

## Same names as in the next classes

```{r}
# rename(new_name = old_name)
here("data", "gapminder.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names() |>
  rename(population = pop, income = gdp_percap) |>
  glimpse()
```

# 2. Add the continent {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**The package `countrycode`**

---

## The file has no continent column

`countrycode()` turns a country name into a continent.

```{r}
# One name in, one continent out
countrycode("Latvia", origin = "country.name", destination = "continent")

# A vector of names works too
countrycode(c("Chile", "Japan", "Kenya"), origin = "country.name", destination = "continent")
```

Three arguments: the names, `origin` (what we have), `destination` (what we want).

---

## mutate() adds the continent to every row

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names() |>
  rename(population = pop, income = gdp_percap) |>
  mutate(
    continent = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", destination = "continent")
  ) |>
  select(country, continent, year, life_exp) |>
  head(4)
```

---

## A finer split: the UN subregion

```{r}
# Same function, another destination
here("data", "gapminder.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names() |>
  rename(population = pop, income = gdp_percap) |>
  mutate(
    continent = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", destination = "continent"),
    subregion = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", destination = "un.regionsub.name")
  ) |>
  distinct(country, continent, subregion) |>
  head(6)
```

---

## Did every country find a continent?

```{r}
# Rows here are countries that countrycode did not recognise
here("data", "gapminder.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    continent = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", destination = "continent")
  ) |>
  filter(is.na(continent)) |>
  distinct(country)
```

An empty table means every name matched.

---

## Save the table for the next classes

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names() |>
  rename(population = pop, income = gdp_percap) |>
  mutate(
    continent = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", destination = "continent"),
    subregion = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", destination = "un.regionsub.name"),
    .after = country
  ) |>
  write_csv(here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv"))
```

From here on we read `gapminder_regions.csv`.

# 3. Split, apply, combine {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Summarize by group**

---

## Three words, three steps

| Step | Word | dplyr |
|------|------|-------|
| 1 | **Split** the rows into groups | `group_by()` |
| 2 | **Apply** a summary to each group | `summarize()` |
| 3 | **Combine** the results in one table | dplyr does it |

---

## Six countries, three continents

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007, country %in% c("Chile", "Argentina", "Japan", "China", "Kenya", "Nigeria")) |>
  select(country, continent, life_exp)
```

---

## Split by continent, apply the mean

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007, country %in% c("Chile", "Argentina", "Japan", "China", "Kenya", "Nigeria")) |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarize(mean_life = mean(life_exp))
```

Six rows became three. Each row is one group.

---

## The shortest summary: count()

```{r}
# How many countries per continent in 2007?
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  count(continent)
```

---

## summarize() alone gives one row

```{r}
# One number for the whole world
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  summarize(mean_life = mean(life_exp))
```

---

## Add group_by() to get one row per group

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarize(mean_life = mean(life_exp))
```

---

## How many countries are behind each mean?

```{r}
# n() counts the rows of each group
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarize(
    mean_life = mean(life_exp),
    n = n()
  )
```

---

## A mean of countries or a mean of people?

```{r}
# weighted.mean() counts each country by its population
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarize(
    mean_life = mean(life_exp),
    weighted_life = weighted.mean(life_exp, population)
  )
```

**Ask:** Which one describes a continent better? Why do they differ?

## Two groups: continent and year

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  group_by(continent, year) |>
  summarize(life_exp = weighted.mean(life_exp, population)) |>
  head(4)
```

Look at the header: `# Groups: continent`. The table is still grouped.

---

## .groups = "drop" removes the grouping

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  group_by(continent, year) |>
  summarize(
    life_exp = weighted.mean(life_exp, population),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  head(4)
```

---

## arrange() ranks the summary

```{r}
# Subregions with the highest life expectancy in 2007
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  group_by(subregion) |>
  summarize(life_exp = weighted.mean(life_exp, population)) |>
  arrange(desc(life_exp)) |>
  head(5)
```

---

# 4. Plot the summary {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**The summary table goes straight into ggplot**

---

## A summary table into a line plot

```{r}
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  group_by(continent, year) |>
  summarize(life_exp = weighted.mean(life_exp, population), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, color = continent)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1)
```

---

## A summary table into a bar chart

```{r}
# The table already holds the values, so we use geom_col()
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarize(life_exp = weighted.mean(life_exp, population)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = continent, y = life_exp)) +
  geom_col()
```

---

## The bars follow the alphabet. How to sort them?

```{r}
# fct_reorder(what to sort, what to sort by)
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarize(life_exp = weighted.mean(life_exp, population)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(continent, life_exp), y = life_exp)) +
  geom_col()
```

---

## Recap {.smaller}

| Task | Code |
|------|------|
| Add a column from a lookup | `mutate(continent = countrycode(...))` |
| Count rows per group | `count(continent)` |
| Summary per group | `group_by()` + `summarize()` |
| Weight by population | `weighted.mean(life_exp, population)` |
| Remove the grouping | `.groups = "drop"` |
| Sort a table | `arrange(desc(...))` |
| Sort bars | `fct_reorder(x, y)` |
